set.item.lead_in: Which of the following signaling responses normally increases the water permeability of collecting-duct principal cells and is impaired in this patient?
set.explanation.distractor_explanations.D: Incorrect for the specified water-permeability response. Vasopressin also regulates inner-medullary urea transport, so that process is not independent of V2 signaling. Urea handling supports the medullary osmotic gradient, whereas the response asked here is cAMP/PKA-mediated insertion of apical AQP2 water channels in principal cells.

set.item.lead_in: Which mechanism most directly accounts for the iron overload caused by this patient's HFE genotype?
set.item.options.D: Repeated red-cell transfusions delivering excess iron to the body
set.item.options.E: Defective DMT1-mediated endosomal iron transport in erythroblasts
set.explanation.distractor_explanations.D: Incorrect. Repeated red-cell transfusions can cause secondary iron overload, but transfusional iron delivery is not the regulatory defect caused by HFE p.Cys282Tyr homozygosity.
set.explanation.distractor_explanations.E: Incorrect. SLC11A2/DMT1 dysfunction impairs erythroblast iron utilization and can produce hypochromic microcytic anemia with hepatic iron overload. It is not the HFE-hepcidin regulatory defect specified in this patient.
